Job Number: R0251312

Data Scientist, Mid

The Opportunity:

Are you excited at the prospect of unlocking the secrets held by a data set? Are you fascinated by the possibilities presented by the IoT, machine learning, and artificial intelligence advances? In an increasingly connected world, massive amounts of structured and unstructured data open up new opportunities. As a data scientist, you can turn these complex data sets into useful information to solve global challenges. Across private and public sectors, from fraud detection to cancer research, to national intelligence, you know the answers are in the data.

We have an opportunity for you to use your leadership and analytical skills to support an intelligence community (IC) agency's collection and analysis operations. You’ll work closely with your customer to understand their questions and needs, then dig into their data-rich environment to find the pieces of their information puzzle. You’ll write scripts to integrate data, conduct exploratory data analysis to discover hidden patterns, apply machine learning to train predictive models, and use the right combination of tools to turn that set of disparate data points into objective answers to help mission partners make informed decisions. You’ll provide your customer with a deep understanding of their data, what it all means, and how they can use it. Join us as we use data science for good in support of the IC’s global mission.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

• 2+ years of experience in data science, including performing quantitative analysis, developing visualizations, and processing complex data to create data-driven insights
• Experience using Python to manipulate and analyze data
• Experience using SQL to conduct complex database queries
• Experience using data manipulation and extract, transform, and load (ETL) procedures
• Experience developing data visualizations, dashboards, or lightweight Web applications to communicate key insights
• Experience communicating information to an audience with varying technical knowledge and expertise in oral or written formats
• TS/SCI clearance
• Bachelor's degree

Nice If You Have:

• Experience using Apache Spark to aggregate and analyze large data sets from various sources
• Experience using the Joint Enterprise Modeling and Analytics (JEMA) framework to develop data processing workflows
• Experience developing Web services or Web applications using Python and Flask or JavaScript
• Experience working with AI and ML technologies and data systems
• Experience applying supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms for clustering, classification, and dimensionality reduction
• Experience working with multiple file types, including geospatial file formats, JSON, and XML
• Experience leveraging APIs to query systems
• Knowledge of commercial Cloud services used by the IC
• Master's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science or Data Analytics

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; TS/SCI clearance is required.

Redhorse transforms the way government uses data and technology. To support this vital mission, we are seeking an executive-level Mid-Level Data Scientist to support the National Security Branch (NSB) and executive-level priority programs.

In this role, you will be at the forefront of modernizing national security missions by designing and deploying advanced machine learning models, custom algorithms, and data workflows across complex law enforcement, intelligence, investigative, and business datasets. • Design, test, and validate the quality, integrity, and performance of data and automated data processes.
• Coordinate across functional teams to deploy predictive models and monitor operational outcomes.
• Analyze findings and present actionable, data-driven recommendations to executive leadership.
• Develop visualizations, infographics, and charts to communicate results and derived findings effectively to non-technical audiences.

Required Experience/Clearance
• 6 years of experience as a Data Scientist or equivalent data-centric role (e.g., Data Analyst, Data Engineer).
• 6 years of experience utilizing multiple programming languages and statistical packages, alongside modern dataset and Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) tools.
• 6 years of experience utilizing data systems to acquire, extract, and prepare data for research, exploration, or statistical analysis.
• 6 years of experience conducting exploratory data analysis to interpret complex data trends and anomalies.
• 6 years of experience cleaning, manipulating, munging, and sub-setting large datasets for analytical workflows.
• 6 years of demonstrated experience communicating technical analysis and findings to non-technical stakeholders using summary visualizations and tables.
• Demonstrated ability to learn rapidly and operate effectively both independently and within cross-functional team environments.
• Ability to obtain and maintain the required U.S. Government Security Clearance suitable for National Security Branch (NSB) programs.

Desired Experience
We encourage all candidates who meet the basic requirements to apply, even if you do not have any of the following experience:

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, Physical Sciences, or a relevant analytical discipline.
• Experience applying the latest technologies and methodologies in data mining, predictive analytics, and machine learning to correlate disparate data sets and investigative events.
• Advanced Python programming proficiency and clean code development utilizing common machine learning frameworks and data science libraries.
• Advanced SQL and database management experience, including writing complex queries, optimizing database operations, and architecting basic ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) pipelines.
• Practical experience developing, training, and tuning both supervised and unsupervised machine learning models.
• Experience designing interactive BI dashboards and presentation-ready visual analytics for senior government leaders.
• Experience using version control systems (such as Git) to manage collaborative code repositories.

Data Scientist/Engineer — Public Trust — Washington, DC (5 days a week onsite)

This hybrid role combines strong data engineering capabilities with advanced data science and machine learning expertise. • Implement MLOps practices including model versioning, CI/CD for ML, containerization, and monitoring of production models.

Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering or related quantitative field.
• 5+ years' experience working in a hybrid Data Scientist and Data Engineer capacity.
• Advanced proficiency in Python and strong command of SQL for complex data querying and manipulation.
• Hands on experience with big data processing frameworks like Apache Spark or Databricks, and workflow orchestration tools like Apache Airflow.
• Solid understanding of data warehousing, lakehouse architectures, and designing scalable ETL/ELT pipelines.

What are Trust Fund Positions?

Trust Fund positions are unique to the Smithsonian. They are paid for from a variety of sources, including the Smithsonian endowment, revenue from our business activities, donations, grants and contracts. Trust employees are not part of the civil service, nor does trust fund employment lead to Federal status. The salary ranges for trust positions are generally the same as for federal positions and in many cases trust and federal employees work side by side. Trust employees have their own benefit program, which may include Health, Dental & Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Transit/Commuter Benefits, Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance, Annual and Sick Leave, Family Friendly Leave, 403b Retirement Plan, Discounts for Smithsonian Memberships, Museum Stores and Restaurants, Credit Union, Smithsonian Early Enrichment Center (Child Care), Flexible Spending Account (Health & Dependent Care).

Conditions of Employment

• Pass Pre-employment Background Check and Subsequent Background Investigation for position designated.

• Complete a Probationary Period.

• Maintain a Bank Account for Direct Deposit/Electronic Transfer.

• The position is open to all candidates eligible to work in the United States. Proof of eligibility to work in U.S. is not required to apply.

• Applicants must meet all qualification and eligibility requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement.

OVERVIEW
This position is located in Washington, DC, within the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO), Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI), under the Office of the Under Secretary for Science and Research at the Smithsonian Institution (SI).

STRI provides a global platform for research on tropical forests and marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and human well-being.

The ForestGEO program is a global network of scientists and forest research sites dedicated to advancing the long-term study of the world's forests.

The GEO-TREES initiative builds on this network to improve the accuracy and verification of global forest carbon estimates through collaboration among forest research sites worldwide. The Data Scientist supports the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) and GEO-TREES programs as a liaison between site-based data collection and the development of analytical data products.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Data Management, Scientific Analysis, and Software Programming (50%)

• Performs data-management, computational, and bioinformatics assignments supporting research in tropical biology, ecology, and forestry.

• Develops, implements, modifies, and maintains data-processing pipelines used to process plot-based tree inventory and related ecological data and to derive estimates such as forest woody biomass density.

• Evaluates the performance of existing data-processing pipelines and recommends modifications or improvements based on data characteristics, analytical requirements, user needs, and experience working with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES site teams.

• Develops and modifies computational procedures for analysis of ForestGEO and GEO-TREES scientific data using established data-science principles, methods, and practices.

• Processes, validates, organizes, and manages tree inventory, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS), and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data for scientific analysis and long-term storage.

• Supports the archiving and long-term management of scientific datasets to ensure appropriate organization, documentation, accessibility, and usability.

• Develops and maintains data-management solutions and informatics workflows for data acquisition, formatting, validation, processing, analysis, use, and storage.

• Implements established data standards and contributes to the development and modification of data structures and architectures appropriate to assigned projects.

• Writes, tests, documents, troubleshoots, and maintains computer code used in data-processing and analytical workflows.

• Uses programming languages and tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, GIS applications, and related scientific and data-management software.

• Identifies data-quality problems, inconsistencies, missing values, formatting issues, and other anomalies and determines appropriate methods for correcting or documenting them.

• Works with researchers and other technical personnel to ensure that processed data and analyticalproducts meet established scientific and program requirements.

• Works closely with researchers and program personnel to identify data-processing, analytical, software, and data-management requirements for assigned scientific projects.

• Conducts technical analyses of available methods and alternatives and recommends appropriate software tools, workflows, calculations, and analytical approaches.

• Assists researchers in translating scientific requirements into practical data-processing and

• computational solutions.

• Evaluates existing workflows and recommends modifications when established approaches do not fully address the characteristics of the data or requirements of an assigned project.

• Coordinates with site representatives concerning timelines and technical requirements for acquisition and submission of plot inventory, TLS, ALS, GNSS, and related scientific data.

• Reviews submitted data to determine whether established ForestGEO and GEO-TREES formatting, documentation, and data-quality requirements have been met.

• Works with site personnel to resolve routine and moderately complex data-submission and data-quality problems.

• Prepares technical documentation describing data-processing workflows, code, data structures, analytical procedures, and related methods.

• Assists in testing new or modified software tools, workflows, and procedures prior to implementation.

Training and Collaboration (25%)

• Develops and provides formal and informal training to researchers, site personnel, and program partners concerning ForestGEO and GEO-TREES data systems, data-management procedures, formatting requirements, data-processing workflows, and related tools.

• Serves as a technical point of contact for tree-inventory teams and other users at assigned ForestGEO and GEO-TREES sites.

• Provides advice, training, troubleshooting assistance, and technical support concerning data collection, formatting, cleaning, validation, processing, documentation, and submission.

• Explains data standards, analytical procedures, software requirements, and data-management practices to researchers and partners with varying levels of technical expertise.

• Collaborates with scientists, data managers, programmers, and other personnel to identify and resolve data-management and processing problems.

• Participates in meetings, working groups, and collaborative activities involving ForestGEO, GEO-TREES, Smithsonian staff, and domestic and international research partners.

• Shares information concerning lessons learned, recurring data problems, workflow improvements, and effective data-management practices with program staff and partners.

Performs other duties as assigned.

• Knowledge of data acquisition, data cleaning, validation, transformation, integration, storage, analysis, visualization, documentation, and reproducible computational workflows.

• Knowledge of computational and data-management methods is required to develop, modify, implement, and maintain processing pipelines for tree inventory, GNSS, ALS, TLS, spatial, and related scientific datasets.

• Knowledge of algorithm development, software testing, version control, debugging, documentation, deployment, and maintenance practices is required to support scientific applications and data-processing workflows.

• Knowledge of the scientific concepts associated with ecology, tropical biology, forestry, or related environmental sciences sufficient to understand data characteristics, research requirements, analytical objectives, and the relationships among data variables.

• Knowledge to select and modify appropriate data-processing and analytical methods; identify and resolve data-quality problems; evaluate alternative computational approaches; interpret results; develop recommendations; and prepare technical documentation and analytical products.

• Skill adapting or modifying established data-science techniques and procedures to address differences in data structure, quality, collection methods, analytical requirements, or site-specific circumstances.

Description

Amazon's Community Intelligence Science & Engineering team operates at the intersection of computational social science, artificial intelligence, and operational excellence. We analyze how Amazon's presence impacts local communities and embed those insights into core operational models. You'll work at the forefront of applied AI and causal inference, building systems that influence decisions affecting thousands of communities daily.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape how the world's most customer-centric company builds sustainable relationships with the communities we serve. A successful Data Scientist on our team demonstrates exceptional scientific rigor combined with pragmatic execution. You'll balance breakthrough research with production deployment, collaborate across multiple science organizations, and translate complex analytical findings into actionable insights that influence senior leadership strategy.

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will partner with product teams, scientists, and technical leaders across Last Mile, Middle Mile, WW Ops Security, WW Real Estate, and other organizations to identify opportunities where community intelligence creates multiplicative business impact.

Key job responsibilities

• Design and deploy production ML forecasting systems with extended prediction horizons using multi-modal data sources
• Build and scale AI-powered analytics platforms that process large volumes of unstructured data from diverse sources including social media, traditional media, and internal systems
• Collaborate with operational science teams to integrate analytical insights and predictive signals into existing operational models and decision-making systems
• Build automated causal discovery systems leveraging knowledge graphs, LLMs, and document understanding to uncover relationships between business actions and outcomes
• Develop NLP and GenAI applications including event detection, sentiment analysis, cross-platform clustering, and multilingual insight synthesis
• Partner with engineering teams to productionize models using AWS services (SageMaker, EMR, Lambda, Kinesis, Glue) with clear POC-to-production handoff criteria
• Mentor junior scientists and contribute to building a research culture that balances high-risk, high-reward innovation with reliable product delivery
• Author internal and externally-facing scientific publications and technical documents

A day in the life

Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment.

• Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
• Maternity and Parental Leave Options

At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

About The Team

Amazon Community Operations (CommOps) works to anticipate our communities’ needs and build positive net impact anywhere we operate. From Operational Excellence to Community Outreach, Community Operations is defining what it means to be a positive presence in the community. This is a fast-paced, start-up environment where creative problem solving, operational excellence, and building relationships are the core of our day-to-day work.

Basic Qualifications

• 5+ years of data querying languages (e.g. SQL), scripting languages (e.g. Python) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g. R, SAS, Matlab, etc.) experience
• 4+ years of data scientist experience

• Knowledge of AWS tech stack (e.g., AWS Redshift, S3, EC2, Glue)

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with data scripting languages (e.g., SQL, Python, R, or equivalent) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g., R, SAS, Matlab, or equivalent)
• Experience managing data pipelines
• Experience as a leader and mentor on a data science team
• Experience documenting modeling for technical and business leaders
• Experience using AI-assisted development tools in academic or professional settings
• Experience contributing to publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals

About Peregrine
Peregrine Advisors is a rapidly growing AI and data innovation hub helping government solve hard problems and deliver better outcomes. We work across the full lifecycle—from strategy and governance through architecture, engineering, analytics, AI, visualization, and training—for clients including the SEC, PCAOB, DDOT, and DCAA.

Our clients describe our support as “absolutely excellent” and our people as “instrumental to organization’s success.” Winner of the United Nations COP27 Datathon, our work has earned all Exceptional CPARS ratings, SEC Chair’s Awards, the SEC Vision Award, and recognition from FDA leadership.

We are also built differently. Peregrine is the first and only social enterprise organized as a Benefit Corporation and SBA 8(a) company focused on AI and data for government. We believe business success should create client value, social value, and opportunity for our people.

As we enter our next stage of growth, we need dependable, motivated, and skilled people who have a combination of intellectual curiosity and intellectual courage. With new clients, larger programs, and expanding responsibilities, the people joining Peregrine now will have the opportunity to help shape the company we become.
People first. Ownership always.
We solve problems through people, process, and technology—in that order. Technology matters, but people make transformation happen. That principle defines our culture. Trust and motivation are the foundational pillars of delivery on which our skills stand. We hire people we can trust, who care deeply about what they do, take ownership, learn quickly, help one another, and refuse to walk past a problem because it belongs to someone else.

At Peregrine, you are not joining simply to fill a position. You are joining a team, taking ownership of a mission, and helping build a company. If that excites you, we should talk.

At Peregrine Advisors, you will carry analytical questions for a federal agency from the data to a defensible, documented answer. But we hire people, not seats. As the work evolves, you will move to where the hardest problems are.

This is a remote position, although a hybrid arrangement based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area with openness to a variable commuting cadence is preferred. Wherever you work from, occasional travel to DC is part of the job. The initial engagement requires United States citizenship and the ability to obtain a Public Trust determination.
Your first project
Your first project will likely have you transforming client data, structured, semi-structured, and unstructured, into analytic processes and outcomes that help drive mission-critical initiatives. Depending on the assignment, you may:

• Frame analytical questions with the people who own the mission, and turn them into designs that can actually be tested.

• Build analyses and models in Python and Structured Query Language (SQL) on cloud-native data platforms hosted in Amazon Web Services (AWS).

• Build models that earn their place: forecasting, classification, risk scoring, and anomaly detection matched to the question, the data, and the scrutiny a federal decision has to survive.

• Design the evaluation that shows a model is fit for a client environment, with baselines, validation designs, error analysis, documented limits, and documentation that lets someone else verify your results.

• Build analytical features and datasets from large, messy, document-heavy corpora, including text extracted with Amazon Textract and analyzed with foundation models through Amazon Bedrock.

• Harden one-off notebooks into repeatable, reviewed analytical pipelines.

• Put findings in front of decision-makers in plain language, with visuals that carry the argument instead of decorating it.

• Use artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted analysis as standard practice, with language models and coding assistants across the lifecycle and your judgment on top.

Adaptability and a demonstrated capacity to learn new concepts, systems, and tools are what keep you ahead of program needs as projects complete and priorities shift.
Who you are
You are rigorous about method and honest about uncertainty: when the evidence supports a narrower claim, you make the narrower claim. You care what the data is for, not just what it contains, and you would rather spend a day understanding the process that produced a number than a week modeling it wrong. You experiment, fail, learn, and repeat quickly. You would rather own an outcome than be handed a task.
What you bring

• A working command of statistics and machine learning applied to real operational data, not just curated coursework sets.

• The engineering habits that make analysis trustworthy: version control, reproducible pipelines, tested transformations, and documentation someone else can follow.

• The communication craft to make a technical result understandable to the people who depend on it.

• The precision to work where accuracy and auditability are not optional.

When we talk
Be prepared to discuss a difficult problem you worked through, the decisions you made, what happened, and what you learned.
What we offer
You will work alongside developers, engineers, data scientists, architects, and strategists, on work ranging from strategy to implementation. We support your development across assignments and clients through extensive onboarding, sponsored professional certifications such as the Data Management Capability Assessment Model (DCAM) and AWS technical certifications, and rotation across functions to expand your skills and perspective. The mission is real, the problems are hard, and you own what you ship.
What we commit to
As a Benefit Corporation, our commitment runs three ways: real, measurable value for our clients; government that works better for the public; and a team that makes everyone in it better.

We hire people who want to help build the firm, not just work at it. If that is you, apply.

Peregrine Advisors is an equal opportunity employer.

Peregrine exclusively works with OPEN Data Jobs to recruit our team. Register with OPEN Data Jobs to be considered for this and future openings.

Requirements

• 4+ years of applied data science or statistical modeling experience

• Bachelor's degree

• Strong working command of Python and SQL

• Working knowledge of statistics, machine learning, and model validation

• Familiarity with cloud-based data and analytics services on AWS

• Ability to carry an analysis from question to defensible, documented answer

• Proficiency in writing, PowerPoint, and Excel

Preferred

• Master's degree in a relevant field

• Experience with modern data tools and platforms (Amazon Aurora, Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) with Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue, or Trino)

• Experience applying large language models to analytical work (Amazon Bedrock or comparable services)

• Data-visualization craft, from chart design through dashboards and charting libraries

• Federal information technology experience

• Familiarity with AI-assisted developer tooling

Benefits

This is a full-time W-2 position with a salary of $78,000 to $147,000 per year.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance with the employee premium fully paid and half of dependent premiums; employer-paid life, accidental death, and short-term and long-term disability insurance; a 401(k) matched 100% up to 4% of salary, vesting immediately; unlimited paid time off; and sponsored professional certifications and continuing education.
